WKBackForwardList.doc: An object that manages the list of previously loaded webpages, which the web view uses for forward and backward navigation.

WKBackForwardListItem.doc: A representation of a webpage that the web view previously visited.

WKContentRuleList.doc: A compiled list of rules to apply to web content.

WKContentRuleListStore.doc: An object that contains the rules for how to load and filter content in the web view.

WKContentWorld.doc: An object that defines a scope of execution for JavaScript code, and which you use to prevent conflicts between different scripts.

WKDownload.doc: An object that represents the download of a web resource.

WKFindConfiguration.doc: The configuration parameters to use when searching the contents of the web view.

WKFindResult.doc: An object that contains the results of searching the web view’s contents.

WKFrameInfo.doc: An object that contains information about a frame on a webpage.

WKHTTPCookieStore.doc: An object that manages the HTTP cookies associated with a particular web view.

WKNavigation.doc: An object that tracks the loading progress of a webpage.

WKNavigationAction.doc: An object that contains information about an action that causes navigation to occur.

WKNavigationResponse.doc: An object that contains the response to a navigation request, and which you use to make navigation-related policy decisions.

WKOpenPanelParameters.doc: The configuration details of a file upload control in your web content.

WKPDFConfiguration.doc: The configuration data to use when generating a PDF representation of a web view’s contents.

WKPreferences.doc: An object that encapsulates the standard behaviors to apply to websites.

WKProcessPool.doc: An opaque token that you use to run multiple web views in a single process.

WKScriptMessage.doc: An object that encapsulates a message sent by JavaScript code from a webpage.

WKSecurityOrigin.doc: An object that identifies the origin of a particular resource.

WKSnapshotConfiguration.doc: The configuration data to use when generating an image from a web view’s contents.

WKUserContentController.doc: An object for managing interactions between JavaScript code and your web view, and for filtering content in your web view.

WKUserScript.doc: A script that the web view injects into a webpage.

WKWebExtension.doc: An object that encapsulates a web extension’s resources that the manifest file defines.

WKWebExtensionContext.doc: An object that represents the runtime environment for a web extension.

WKWebExtensionController.doc: An object that manages a set of loaded extension contexts.

WKWebView.doc: An object that displays interactive web content, such as for an in-app browser.

WKWebViewConfiguration.doc: A collection of properties that you use to initialize a web view.

WKWebpagePreferences.doc: An object that specifies the behaviors to use when loading and rendering page content.

WKWebsiteDataRecord.doc: A record of the data that a particular website stores persistently.

WKWebsiteDataStore.doc: An object that manages cookies, disk and memory caches, and other types of data for a web view.

WKWindowFeatures.doc: Display-related attributes that a webpage requests for its window.

WebArchive.doc: A WebArchive object represents a webpage that can be archived—for example, archived on disk or on the pasteboard. A WebArchive object contains the main resource, as well as the subresources and subframes of the main resource. The main resource can be an entire webpage, a portion of a webpage, or some other kind of data such as an image. Use this class to archive webpages, or place a portion of a webpage on the pasteboard, or to represent rich web content in any application.

WebBackForwardList.doc: A WebBackForwardList object maintains a list of visited pages used to go back and forward to the most recent page. A WebBackForwardList object maintains only the list data—it does not perform actual page loads (in other words, it does not make any client requests). If you need to perform a page load, see the loadRequest: method in WebFrame to find out how to do this.

WebDataSource.doc: WebDataSource encapsulates the web content to be displayed in a web frame view. A WebDataSource object has a representation object, conforming to the WebDocumentRepresentation protocol, that holds the data in an appropriate format depending on the MIME type. You can extend WebKit to support new MIME types by implementing your own view and representation classes, and specifying the mapping between them using the registerViewClass:representationClass:forMIMEType: WebView class method.

WebDownload.doc: WebDownload objects initiate download client requests on behalf of a delegate. A download request involves loading the data, decoding it (if necessary), and saving it to a file. Instances of this class behave similar to NSURLDownload except delegates of WebDownload may implement an additional delegate method. The method allows the delegate to specify the window to be used for authentication sheets. If the delegate does not implement this method, the WebDownload object will prompt the user for authentication using the standard WebKit authentication panel, as either a sheet or window. There are no additional methods defined in this class. See WebDownloadDelegate for the delegate method.

WebFrame.doc: A WebFrame object encapsulates the data displayed in a WebFrameView object. There is one WebFrame object per frame displayed in a WebView. An entire webpage is represented by a hierarchy of WebFrame objects in which the root object is called the main frame.

WebFrameView.doc: WebFrameView objects and their subviews display the web content contained in a frame. You never create instances of WebFrameView directly—WebView objects create and manage a hierarchy of WebFrameView objects, one for each frame. WebFrameView objects use a scroll view whose document view conforms to the WebDocumentView protocol.

WebHistory.doc: WebHistory objects are used to maintain the pages visited by users. Visited pages are represented by WebHistoryItem objects. You add and remove history items using the addItems: and removeItems: methods. These methods post appropriate notifications when items are added or removed so you can update the display. WebHistory organizes the WebHistoryItem objects by the day they were visited, ordered from most recent to oldest. You can request all the days that contain history items using the orderedLastVisitedDays method or request the items visited on a particular day using the orderedItemsLastVisitedOnDay: method. WebHistory objects can be loaded and saved by specifying a file URL (see loadFromURL:error:).

WebHistoryItem.doc: WebHistoryItem objects encapsulate information about visiting a page so that users can return to that page. WebHistory and WebBackForwardList objects manage lists of WebHistoryItem objects. WebHistoryItem objects are created and added to these lists automatically when loading pages, so you do not need to create WebHistoryItem objects directly.

WebPreferences.doc: WebPreferences encapsulates the preferences you can change per WebView object. These preferences include font, text encoding, and image settings. Normally a WebView object uses the standard preferences returned by the standardPreferences class method. However, you can modify the preferences for individual WebView instances too. Use the preferencesIdentifier WebView method to change a WebView object’s preferences, or to share preferences between WebView objects. Use the autosaves method to specify if the preferences object should be automatically saved to the user defaults database.

WebResource.doc: A WebResource object represents a downloaded URL. It encapsulates the data of the download as well as other resource properties such as the URL, MIME type, and frame name.

WebScriptObject.doc: A WebScriptObject object is an Objective-C wrapper for a scripting object passed to your application from the scripting environment.

WebUndefined.doc: WebUndefined objects are simply used to represent the JavaScript “undefined” value in methods when bridging between JavaScript and Objective-C. For example, if you invoke a JavaScript function that returns the JavaScript “undefined” value, then a WebUndefined object is returned to the Objective-C calling context.

WKDownloadDelegate.doc: A protocol you implement to track download progress and handle redirects, authentication challenges, and failures.

WKHTTPCookieStoreObserver.doc: The methods to adopt in an object that monitors changes to a webpage’s cookies.

WKNavigationDelegate.doc: Methods for accepting or rejecting navigation changes, and for tracking the progress of navigation requests.

WKScriptMessageHandler.doc: An interface for receiving messages from JavaScript code running in a webpage.

WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply.doc: An interface for responding to messages from JavaScript code running in a webpage.

WKUIDelegate.doc: The methods for presenting native user interface elements on behalf of a webpage.

WKURLSchemeHandler.doc: A protocol for loading resources with URL schemes that WebKit doesn’t handle.

WKURLSchemeTask.doc: An interface that WebKit uses to request custom resources from your app.

WKWebExtensionControllerDelegate.doc: A group of methods you use to customize web extension interactions.

WKWebExtensionTab.doc: A protocol with methods that represent a tab to web extensions.

WKWebExtensionWindow.doc: A protocol with methods that represent a window to web extensions.

WebDocumentRepresentation.doc: This protocol is adopted by document representation classes that handle specific MIME types. You can implement your own document view classes and document representation classes to render data for specific MIME types, and register those classes using the WebFrame registerViewClass:representationClass:forMIMEType: method.

WebDocumentSearching.doc: WebDocumentSearching is an optional protocol for document view objects that support searching. Classes that adopt this protocol should also adopt WebDocumentView and inherit from NSView.

WebDocumentText.doc: WebDocumentText is an optional protocol for document view objects that display text. This protocol defines methods for accessing document content as strings, and methods for text selection. Classes that adopt this protocol should also adopt WebDocumentView and inherit from NSView.

WebDocumentView.doc: This protocol is adopted by the document view of a WebFrameView. You can extend WebKit to support additional MIME types by implementing your own document view and document representation classes to render data for specific MIME types. You register those classes using the WebFrame registerViewClass:representationClass:forMIMEType: method. Classes that adopt this protocol are expected to be subclasses of NSView.

WebDownloadDelegate.doc: The WebDownloadDelegate protocol declares one additional method for delegates of WebDownload.

WebOpenPanelResultListener.doc: WebView user interface delegates that implement the webView:runOpenPanelForFileButtonWithResultListener: method use the methods defined in this protocol to communicate with the listener object. The methods allow the delegate to send a cancel message, or set the selected file name.

WebPolicyDecisionListener.doc: This protocol enables WebView policy delegates to communicate with listener objects. A listener object conforming to this protocol is passed as one of the arguments to web view policy delegate methods.

WebResourceLoadDelegate.doc: Web view resource load delegates implement this protocol to be notified on the progress of loading individual resources. Note that there can be hundreds of resources, such as images and other media, per page. So, if you just want to get page loading status see the WebFrameLoadDelegate protocol.

WebUIDelegate.doc: Web view user interface delegates implement this protocol to control the opening of new windows, augment the behavior of default menu items displayed when the user clicks elements, and perform other user interface–related tasks. These methods can be invoked as a result of handling JavaScript or other plug-in content. Delegates that display more than one web view per window, for example, need to implement some of these methods to handle that case. The default implementation assumes one window per web view, so non-conventional user interfaces might implement a user interface delegate.

WKAudiovisualMediaTypes.doc: The media types that require a user gesture to begin playing.

WKAudiovisualMediaTypeAll.doc: All media types require a user gesture to begin playing.

WKAudiovisualMediaTypeAudio.doc: Media types that contain audio require a user gesture to begin playing.

WKAudiovisualMediaTypeNone.doc: No media types require a user gesture to begin playing.

WKAudiovisualMediaTypeVideo.doc: Media types that contain video require a user gesture to begin playing.

WKContentMode.doc: Constants that indicate how to render web view content.

WKCookiePolicy.doc: An enumeration with cases that indicate whether a cookie store allows cookie storage.

WKDialogResult.doc: An enumeration that lists the possible ways a delegate handled displaying a custom Lockdown Mode first use dialog.

WKDialogResultAskAgain.doc: A result that indicates the delegate didn’t display a message, so other web views should check again.

WKDialogResultHandled.doc: A result that indicates the delegate displayed the first use message.

WKDialogResultShowDefault.doc: A result that indicates the delegate didn’t display a message, so the web view should show the default Lockdown Mode message.

WKDownloadRedirectPolicy.doc: An enumeration with cases that indicate whether to proceed with a redirect.

WKErrorCode.doc: Possible error values that WebKit APIs can return.

WKInactiveSchedulingPolicy.doc: An enumeration that lists policies for how a web view that’s not in a window handles tasks.

WKMediaCaptureState.doc: An enumeration that describes whether a media device, like a camera or microphone, is currently capturing audio or video.

WKMediaCaptureStateActive.doc: The media device is actively capturing audio or video.

WKMediaCaptureStateMuted.doc: The media device is muted, and not actively capturing audio or video.

WKMediaCaptureType.doc: An enumeration listing the types of media devices that can capture audio, video, or both.

WKMediaCaptureTypeCamera.doc: A media device that can capture video.

WKMediaCaptureTypeCameraAndMicrophone.doc: A media device or devices that can capture audio and video.

WKMediaCaptureTypeMicrophone.doc: A media device that can capture audio.

WKMediaPlaybackState.doc: An enumeration that describes whether an audio or video presentation is playing, paused, or suspended.

WKMediaPlaybackStateNone.doc: There is no media to play back.

WKMediaPlaybackStateSuspended.doc: The media is not playing, and cannot be resumed until the user revokes the suspension.

WKNavigationActionPolicy.doc: Constants that indicate whether to allow or cancel navigation to a webpage from an action.

WKNavigationResponsePolicy.doc: Constants that indicate whether to allow or cancel navigation to a webpage from a response.

WKNavigationType.doc: The type of action that triggered the navigation.

WKNavigationTypeBackForward.doc: A request for the frame’s next or previous item.

WKNavigationTypeFormResubmitted.doc: A request to resubmit a form.

WKNavigationTypeFormSubmitted.doc: A request to submit a form.

WKNavigationTypeOther.doc: A navigation request that originates for some other reason.

WKNavigationTypeReload.doc: A request to reload the webpage.

WKPermissionDecision.doc: An enumeration of possible permission decisions for device resource access.

WKPermissionDecisionDeny.doc: Deny permission for the requested resource.

WKPermissionDecisionGrant.doc: Grant permission for the requested resource.

WKPermissionDecisionPrompt.doc: Prompt the user for permission for the requested resource.

WKUserInterfaceDirectionPolicy.doc: The policy that determines the directionality of user interface elements in a web view.

WKUserInterfaceDirectionPolicyContent.doc: The directionality follows the CSS/HTML/XHTML specifications.

WKUserInterfaceDirectionPolicySystem.doc: The directionality follows the view’s user interface layout direction.

WKUserScriptInjectionTime.doc: Constants for the times at which to inject script content into a webpage.

WKUserScriptInjectionTimeAtDocumentEnd.doc: A constant to inject the script after the document finishes loading, but before loading any other subresources.

WKUserScriptInjectionTimeAtDocumentStart.doc: A constant to inject the script after the creation of the webpage’s document element, but before loading any other content.

WKWebExtensionDataRecordError.doc: Constants that indicate errors in the WKWebExtensionDataRecord domain.

WKWebExtensionMatchPatternError.doc: Constants that indicate errors in the WKWebExtensionMatchPattern domain.

WKWebExtensionMatchPatternOptions.doc: Constants used by WKWebExtensionMatchPattern to indicate matching options.

WKWebExtensionMessagePortError.doc: Constants that indicate errors in the WKWebExtensionMessagePort domain.

WKWebExtensionWindowState.doc: Constants used by WKWebExtensionWindow to indicate possible states of a window.

WKWebExtensionWindowType.doc: Constants used by WKWebExtensionWindow to indicate the type of a window.

WebCacheModel.doc: Specifies the caching model for a web view.

WebCacheModelDocumentBrowser.doc: Caches a reasonable number of resources and previously viewed documents in memory and on disk. This model is appropriate for displaying and navigating between multiple documents.

WebCacheModelDocumentViewer.doc: Releases resources when they are no longer referenced and caches remote resources on disk. This model is appropriate for displaying a static document with no navigation user interface. This is the most memory-efficient model.

WebCacheModelPrimaryWebBrowser.doc: Caches a large number of resources and previously viewed documents in memory and on disk. This model is appropriate for a web view that behaves like a web browser.

WebDragDestinationAction.doc: Actions that the destination object of a drag operation can perform.

WebDragDestinationActionAny.doc: Allows any defined action to occur.

WebDragDestinationActionDHTML.doc: Allows DHTML (such as JavaScript) to handle the drag.

WebDragDestinationActionEdit.doc: Allows editable documents to be changed by the drag operation.

WebDragDestinationActionLoad.doc: Allows the drag operation to change the location.

WebDragSourceAction.doc: Actions that the source object of a drag operation can perform.

WebDragSourceActionAny.doc: Allows any defined action to occur.

WebDragSourceActionDHTML.doc: Allows DHTML (such as JavaScript) in the source object to initiate a drag operation.

WebDragSourceActionImage.doc: Allows the user to drag an image in the source object.

WebDragSourceActionLink.doc: Allows the user to drag a link in the source object.

WebDragSourceActionSelection.doc: Allows the user to drag a selection in the source object.

WebNavigationType.doc: Possible values for the WebActionNavigationTypeKey key that appears in an action dictionary.

WebNavigationTypeBackForward.doc: The user clicked back or forward button.

WebNavigationTypeFormResubmitted.doc: A form was resubmitted (through a back, forward or reload action).

WebNavigationTypeOther.doc: Navigation is taking place for some other reason.

WebNavigationTypeReload.doc: The user hit the reload button.

WebViewInsertAction.doc: The type of user action that initiated a delegate message.

WebViewInsertActionDropped.doc: Indicates the user inserted content by dropping.

WebViewInsertActionPasted.doc: Indicates the user inserted content by pasting.

WebViewInsertActionTyped.doc: Indicates the user inserted content by typing.
